about.title: San Rafael Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: San Rafael's public-record crash counts show hundreds of injury collisions each year, with a noticeable cluster on Friday afternoons as commuters funnel onto US-101 or navigate the 2nd and 3rd Street corridors downtown. Lincoln Avenue adds another layer of local traffic where intersections and turning movements often factor into reported crashes. If you were hurt in one of these collisions, the days right after matter: insurers may reach out quickly, and what you say to them can shape your claim before you've even seen a doctor. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves — we're a free connection service that matches injured San Rafael residents with an independent personal injury attorney working on contingency. That means no fee unless there's a recovery. Our role is simple: help you find someone who can look at the facts of your crash, explain your options under California law, and take the pressure off while you focus on recovering.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before the Insurer Calls

items.title: California's Two-Year Clock
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a personal injury claim, but that window can shrink to as little as six months if a government entity — like a city road or Caltrans-maintained stretch of US-101 — was involved. An attorney can flag deadlines early so evidence doesn't slip away.

items.title: Comparative Fault Cuts Both Ways
items.desc: California allows recovery even if you share some blame for the crash, but your compensation gets reduced by your percentage of fault. Having someone review the collision report and witness accounts can help make sure fault isn't overstated against you.

items.title: No Cap on Non-Economic Damages
items.desc: California doesn't limit compensation for pain, suffering, or diminished quality of life in most car accident cases. That makes it especially important not to downplay your injuries in a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer before you understand the full extent of your harm.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: It's generally wise to avoid giving a recorded statement before speaking with an attorney. Insurers often use those statements to minimize claims, and something said early — before you know the full scope of your injuries — can be used against you later. An independent attorney can advise you on how to respond.

items.question: What if my accident happened on US-101 or another state-maintained road?
items.answer: If a government entity's road design or maintenance played a role, the claim deadline can be much shorter than the usual two years — sometimes just six months. It's worth having an attorney evaluate this quickly, especially given how much San Rafael traffic funnels through US-101.

items.question: How much does it cost to get connected with an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: Nothing upfront. LawProactive is a free service, and the independent attorneys in our network typically work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no obligation to move forward after you're connected.
